title: Structure of finite groups and the Sylow theorems
summary: The fundamental theorem of finite abelian groups and of finitely generated abelian groups; solvable groups; Cauchy's theorem and the three Sylow theorems with proofs by group actions; applications: groups of order pq, non-simplicity of groups of given orders, and the classification of groups of small order as the final synthesis.

objectives.description: Objectives for this unit will be finalised when it is prepared; the source material is chapters 13 and 15 of Judson with MIT student notes lectures 22–23 as a supplement.

preparation.description: Read Section 13.1: the fundamental theorem of finite abelian groups (Theorem 13.1.4) with Lemmas 13.1.6–13.1.9, and Theorem 13.1.10 for finitely generated abelian groups; then Section 13.2 (solvable groups) from the chapter page.

Read Section 15.1: Cauchy's theorem (Theorem 15.1.1), Corollary 15.1.2, the First Sylow Theorem (Theorem 15.1.4), Lemmas 15.1.5–15.1.6, the Second and Third Sylow Theorems (Theorems 15.1.7–15.1.8); then Section 15.2 (examples, applications, finite simple groups) from the chapter page.
Optional supplement: MIT student notes, lectures 22–23 (The Sylow Theorems; Proofs and Applications).
